title: A bulk 'run all' collector control must exclude non-production collectors by default
requirement: Where a GUI exposes a bulk 'run all collectors' control, it MUST NOT include experimental/soak/non-promoted collectors by default. Only collectors on the production/finalized list (see STD-UI-COM-005) may run as part of a bulk action.
rationale: Consistent across every surveyed Clank that has both a bulk control and a maturity concept: watch-clank's run-all-safe route, korean-tech-wire's production_only=True default, feature-phone-clank's and tablet-clank's and smartwatch-clank's allowlist-scoped run-all. oem-radar's bulk sweep excludes 'heavy' collectors by runtime cost rather than by maturity tier specifically, which is a related but distinct axis — noted as a partial-fit rather than full corroboration.
forbidden: A 'run all' control that iterates every registered collector regardless of maturity
Requiring an env var or config override to exclude experimental collectors from bulk runs (the exclusion must be the default, not opt-in)
acceptance: The bulk-run code path filters to the production/finalized allowlist before iterating
An experimental collector is not run as a side effect of a bulk action without an explicit override

evidence.summary: Bulk run excludes EXPERIMENTAL_MATURITY_COLLECTORS by default, re-enable only via explicit env var.
production_only=(source_id is None) — bulk run is production-only by construction; individual targeting is the only way to reach an EXPERIMENTAL source.
Same allowlist-scoped bulk run in three further SKU-family Clanks.

Partial fit: bulk sweep excludes collectors by runtime cost ('heavy', >5min), a different axis than production/experimental maturity, though genuinely-experimental collectors are separately kept off the GUI catalog entirely.

notes: Pass 1 candidate. chinese-tech-wire has no maturity concept (out of scope, not counter-evidence); semiconductor-intelligence's 'collect all enabled' is opt-in per source rather than maturity-gated and does not clearly corroborate or contradict this rule.
